raw_response:
I'm 63 this year, been farming since I was 15. Never went to school, can't read the words on the fertilizer bags, but I know my land. Eight mu — that's what I have. Five mu I do wheat and then maize right after, that's my main food and money. Two mu is cotton, been doing that for years. And there's one small piece near the house, I put mungbean there — good for porridge, and I can sell a little at the market.

The wheat went in last October, right after National Day, same as always. I put one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu then — the kind with three colors on the bag, my son buys it from the shop in town. Now it's spring and the wheat is greening up. Last year I topdressed half a bag of urea per mu at jointing, got about 400 jin per mu. This year everything costs more, but my neighbor Aunt Wang tried to save money on fertilizer two years ago and her wheat turned yellow and thin. I'll do the same as last year — half a bag of urea per mu when the wheat starts jointing. I can't afford to lose yield. I'll irrigate twice more — once at jointing, once when the grain is filling. Pumping water costs 20-30 yuan each time, electricity isn't cheap, but dry wheat is useless.

For cotton, I plant in late April. I buy new hybrid seed from the shop, about two and a half jin per mu. I put less fertilizer than wheat — about half a bag of compound per mu at planting, then another half bag of urea when the flowers come. Cotton is hard work — pruning, picking. My daughter-in-law helps, and the grandchildren pick after school in autumn. I don't hire workers, too expensive, 150 yuan a day. I'll irrigate twice if the sky stays dry — July and August are the critical times.

Maize is the rush — wheat comes off in early June with the combine, costs me 50 yuan per mu but it's fast. Then maize has to go in within days or the season is lost, no time for deep plowing. I put one bag of compound per mu in the furrow when planting. If the leaves look yellow at the big trumpet stage, I might scatter half a bag of urea. Last year was dry so I watered twice, but if this summer rains like normal, maybe once is enough. I hope for 450 jin per mu.

The mungbean on that one mu — I don't put much into it. A small handful of seed, maybe a little scoop of compound fertilizer. Water it once if the ground cracks. Family eats it. Not much money but it's something.

I need about 4,000 yuan for seeds, fertilizer, pumping, and chemicals this year. My sons work in Shijiazhuang and send some money home, and I have a little saved from last year's grain. I don't want to spend it all — what if someone gets sick? But you have to put money in to get food out. I'll spend what I must and no more. Better to use a bit less fertilizer than to owe money to anyone.
